title: Alex West: Shotgun approach to products, owning data infrastructure, and trust as the moat
summary: Alex West, a bootstrapping solo developer, talks about building many products on shared infrastructure, why he thinks trust and attention win as everything gets commoditized, and how to find and validate ideas. He also covers working in the building phase versus the marketing phase and the Peter Levels shotgun approach.

principles.text: Own reusable data infrastructure and build every product on it so you can ship new ones fast.
principles.quote: everybody should own a data pipeline because I think that the future is or the value of the next economies will or the next economy will be on data

principles.text: Test many products to find traction. Diversify only after you are wealthy, not while chasing your first big win.
principles.quote: I think diversifying is great for retaining your wealth not for making your wealth so I think when you're up and coming you should focus on one thing try to hit the [ __ ] home run

principles.text: Most success stories start with traction, which is what makes founders willing to pull their soul into a product.
principles.quote: I feel that most success stories they start with a bank they start with traction because when you have traction then you're willing to pull your soul into it

principles.text: Building the product is the easy part. Validate demand and market first, then earn, then build.
principles.quote: I launched without even building anything and I reached a hundred dollars per month fast forward another two years later two years into running cyber leads

principles.text: As tech is commoditized and barriers to entry fall, trust and attention are what cannot be copied.
principles.quote: the only thing that cannot be commoditized is Trust and attention you can pay for ads but that is it's a race prices are going to go up as more people join

principles.text: Identical products can win through different positioning, which attracts different customers.
principles.quote: with exactly the same product position in a different way and you will get different customers then they will prefer you
